situation:
You are the store operations lead at CEDARWORKS FURNITURE CO-OPERATIVE, a four-showroom furniture retailer owned by the people who work in it. The general manager (judge), elected by the member-owners, has asked you to evaluate a proposal from a delivery driver and recommend whether Cedarworks should adopt it this quarter.

Cedarworks sells custom sofas and tables built to order by two regional mills. Lead times have stretched from five weeks to nine, and roughly one order in six is now cancelled before it ships. Customers who wait are calling the showrooms for updates the staff cannot give them, and the co-operative has not turned a profit in three quarters.

The driver proposes selling only warehouse and showroom-floor stock, promising two-week delivery and taking no custom orders until the backlog clears. That ends the cancellations this quarter and empties the floors, leaving nothing to show and no mill orders placed for next quarter. The alternative is paying a third mill a premium to cut the backlog, which spends the surplus the members share in December.

The general manager (judge) wants your recommendation on the driver's proposal, and on how you would put whichever course you choose into practice. You will present in the general manager's office. The general manager (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the general manager (judge) will thank you for your work.
